extra.message: Privilege Escalation via Mass Assignment — An authenticated attacker can become an administrator or gain elevated permissions, compromising the entire application. [verified: The update_profile API model in server/api/v1/api_v1.py includes 'role' and 'permissions' fields (lines 42-43) without any visible authorization check in the provided code. No compensating control (e.g., role validation, server-side filtering) is present, so any authenticated user can escalate privileges by updating these fields.]

Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Profile Retrieval — An attacker can view any user's personal information, including email, country, role, and permissions, leading to privacy breaches and reconnaissance. [verified: The profile_query parser accepts a user_id from query parameters without any ownership check; the token_required decorator only authenticates but does not authorize against the requested user_id. Thus an authenticated user can supply any user_id to retrieve another user's PII.]

Debug Mode Enabled in Production — An attacker can leverage error messages to gather information about the application internals, aiding further attacks. [verified: The DEBUG flag is set to True in server/config.py, which enables Flask's debug mode. No custom error handler or environment-specific override is present in provided code, so detailed stack traces will be shown to users on errors, exposing internal paths and schema.]
